about: The shelf. Industries are categories; narratives are subcategories. Tracked narratives live in watchlist.json and carry an `industry` that must match a `name` here. Candidates are claims we expect to pass the admission test (SYSTEM.md §1) but have not collected: no corpus, no stats, no verdicts. A candidate is admitted only after collection shows 3+ independent channels telling it across 2+ months. YouTube category IDs and topicCategories are weak signals for routing search results, never the taxonomy (coders agree with the uploader's category 28% of the time).

candidate_rules.name: Attributed, never asserted: the claim in its believers' words inside quotes, then 'story'. A believer should accept it as a fair statement of what they believe.
candidate_rules.hook: Written only at admission, from data: the tension the corpus can show. Candidates carry no hook.
candidate_rules.frame: Problem, cause, outcome or remedy, and clock (null if the claim carries no date).

industries.name: AI & technology
industries.definition: Claims about what computing, AI and software will do to work, companies and capability.
excludes: AI as an investment bubble (Economy & markets)
AI in film and music (Entertainment & media)
platform and creator issues (Internet & creator economy)
industries.resolves_by: calendar: capability and adoption claims name dates

candidates.name: The "AGI is a year or two away" story
candidates.claim: Human-level artificial general intelligence will arrive within one to two years, so jobs, companies and society must prepare now.

frame.outcome: AGI transforms or replaces most knowledge work

candidates.name: The "AI will take most white-collar jobs" story
candidates.claim: AI will eliminate most entry-level and white-collar office jobs within a few years, and workers should reskill or lose out.

frame.cause: AI models and agents doing office work
frame.outcome: Most office jobs disappear; remedy is reskilling
frame.clock: often 'within 5 years' or a named year

candidates.name: The "quantum computers will break Bitcoin and encryption" story
candidates.claim: Quantum computers will soon break the encryption that secures Bitcoin, banking and the internet.

frame.outcome: Bitcoin and banking security fail unless systems migrate

industries.name: Economy & markets
industries.definition: Claims about where economies, prices, currencies and asset markets are heading.
excludes: personal finance tutorials with no claim
company product news with no market call
industries.resolves_by: calendar: market calls name prices, dates or events

candidates.name: The "recession within six months" story
candidates.claim: A US recession is about to begin, as shown by an inverted yield curve, falling indicators or layoffs.

frame.problem: The US economy is about to contract
frame.cause: Rate hikes, inverted yield curve, weakening consumer
frame.clock: the next 6–12 months, restated each year

candidates.name: The "silver is about to explode" story
candidates.claim: Silver is massively undervalued and a short squeeze or supply shortage will send it to $100 or more.

frame.outcome: Price explodes; remedy is to buy physical silver

candidates.name: The "office real estate will sink the regional banks" story
candidates.claim: Empty offices and falling commercial property values will cause a wave of regional bank failures.

frame.cause: Remote work, high rates, refinancing wall

industries.name: Health & biotech
industries.definition: Claims about what causes disease, what heals it, and what drugs, diets and technologies do to the body.
excludes: workout tutorials with no health claim
medical news with no recurring claim
industries.resolves_by: evidence: graded against the research, never a calendar

candidates.name: The "GLP-1 drugs will end obesity" story
candidates.claim: Ozempic-type GLP-1 drugs are a breakthrough that will end the obesity epidemic; critics say they carry hidden long-term costs.

frame.cause: Appetite biology that willpower can't fix
frame.outcome: Weight-loss drugs as the remedy, contested on safety and rebound

candidates.name: The "microplastics are making us sick" story
candidates.claim: Microplastics now found in blood, brains and organs are a major hidden cause of disease.

frame.cause: Microplastics from bottles, food and packaging

candidates.name: The "ageing can be reversed" story
candidates.claim: Ageing is a disease that can already be slowed or reversed with specific protocols, supplements and therapies.

industries.name: Politics & geopolitics
industries.definition: Claims about wars, elections, states and the balance of power between countries.
industries.resolves_by: calendar: conflict and election claims name dates or events

candidates.name: The "World War III is about to start" story
candidates.claim: Current conflicts are escalating toward a third world war that will begin soon.

candidates.name: The "China will invade Taiwan by 2027" story
candidates.claim: China will invade or blockade Taiwan by 2027.

candidates.name: The "America is heading for civil war" story
candidates.claim: Political division in the United States is heading toward a second civil war.

frame.clock: often tied to the next election

industries.name: Energy & climate
industries.definition: Claims about energy supply, electric vehicles, power grids and the climate.
industries.resolves_by: calendar and evidence: supply and adoption claims name dates; science claims are graded on evidence

candidates.name: The "electric cars are failing" story
candidates.claim: Electric vehicle demand is collapsing and carmakers' EV bets are a costly failure.

candidates.name: The "the grid can't power AI" story
candidates.claim: AI data centres will consume so much electricity that power grids can't keep up, causing blackouts or price spikes.

frame.outcome: Blackouts, price spikes; remedy: nuclear and gas

candidates.name: The "fusion power is finally close" story
candidates.claim: Recent breakthroughs mean commercial fusion power is only years away.

industries.name: Entertainment & media
industries.definition: Claims about film, TV, music, streaming and the businesses behind them.
industries.resolves_by: calendar: box office, subscriber and business claims resolve on results

candidates.name: The "Hollywood is collapsing" story
candidates.claim: The Hollywood studio system is in terminal decline as box office, cable and streaming economics fail.

candidates.name: The "superhero movies are dead" story
candidates.claim: Audiences are tired of superhero films and the genre's era is over.

frame.clock: each major release is a test

candidates.name: The "AI will replace actors and writers" story
candidates.claim: Generative AI will replace actors, writers and musicians in mainstream entertainment.

frame.cause: AI video, voice and script generation
frame.outcome: AI-made films and music replace human work

industries.name: Gaming
industries.definition: Claims about the games industry, platforms and upcoming releases.
industries.resolves_by: calendar: release and business claims resolve on dates

candidates.name: The "GTA 6 will be delayed again" story
candidates.claim: Grand Theft Auto VI will miss its announced release date again.

candidates.name: The "the games industry is collapsing" story
candidates.claim: Layoffs, studio closures and failed releases show the video game industry is in collapse.

candidates.name: The "live-service games are dead" story
candidates.claim: The live-service game model is failing, with most new launches shutting down within months.

frame.cause: Too many competing games, player fatigue

industries.name: Sports
industries.definition: Claims about leagues, money, players and the future of sport.
excludes: match analysis with no recurring claim
industries.resolves_by: calendar: rulings, seasons and ratings resolve on dates

candidates.name: The "Saudi money is taking over sport" story
candidates.claim: Saudi state investment is buying control of football, golf, boxing and other sports.

candidates.name: The "the NBA is losing its audience" story
candidates.claim: NBA viewership is collapsing and the league is losing its fans.

frame.cause: Style of play, load management, streaming

candidates.name: The "the 115 charges will sink Man City" story
candidates.claim: Manchester City will be found guilty on the Premier League's financial charges and face severe punishment.

frame.outcome: Points deduction, titles stripped or relegation

industries.name: Internet & creator economy
industries.definition: Claims about platforms, algorithms, creators and what the internet is becoming.
excludes: creator drama with no recurring claim
industries.resolves_by: calendar and evidence: bans and policy changes resolve on dates; platform claims on evidence

candidates.name: The "dead internet" story
candidates.claim: Most of what's online is now made by bots and AI rather than people.

candidates.name: The "YouTube is killing small creators" story
candidates.claim: YouTube's algorithm suppresses small creators in favour of big channels and advertisers.

candidates.name: The "TikTok is about to be banned" story
candidates.claim: TikTok will be banned in the United States.

industries.name: Fringe & unexplained
industries.definition: Claims about the paranormal, UFOs, lost history and suppressed science.
excludes: horror entertainment with no factual claim
industries.resolves_by: evidence and calendar: factual claims on evidence; disclosure dates on the calendar

candidates.name: The "UFO disclosure is imminent" story
candidates.claim: The US government is about to confirm it holds non-human craft and bodies.

frame.clock: named hearings and dates, repeatedly moved

candidates.name: The "an advanced ice-age civilisation was erased" story
candidates.claim: An advanced civilisation existed before the last ice age and was wiped out, and mainstream archaeology ignores the evidence.

candidates.name: The "that interstellar object is alien technology" story
candidates.claim: Interstellar objects passing through the solar system, such as 'Oumuamua and 3I/ATLAS, may be alien probes.

industries.name: Culture & society
industries.definition: Claims about how people live, relate, raise children and change as societies.
industries.resolves_by: evidence: social claims rarely carry a date

candidates.name: The "falling birth rates will end civilisation" story
candidates.claim: Collapsing birth rates will shrink and age societies until economies and civilisation break down.

frame.cause: Cost of living, culture, delayed family

candidates.name: The "smartphones are rewiring kids' brains" story
candidates.claim: Smartphones and social media caused the rise in teen anxiety and depression.

candidates.name: The "men are falling behind" story
candidates.claim: Young men are falling behind in education, work and relationships, and society is ignoring it.
